links.outcome: Perceived understanding and ease, clarity, comprehensibility ratings of LLM-simplified vs original DTx materials
links.effect: Group×time interaction on perceived understanding: insomnia F=24.8, nicotine F=14.1 (both P<.001), greater gains with LLM-simplified text; ease/clarity/comprehensibility rated higher (r=0.11-0.24). Self-reported outcomes only.
links.quote: A significant group×time interaction was observed in both experiments.

links.outcome: Effect of simplifying patient materials to a 10-11-year-old reading level on perceived understanding and ratings
links.effect: LLM-simplified materials targeted at a 10- to 11-year-old reading level yielded greater perceived understanding gains (P<.001) and higher ease, clarity, comprehensibility ratings (all P<.05, r=0.11-0.24) than originals.
links.quote: In the insomnia experiment, the LLM-simplified explanations were rated significantly higher for ease ( U =27,281; P =.008; r =0.127), clarity ( U =27,803; P =.02; r =0.110), and comprehensibility ( U =25,125; P <.001; r =0.196).

links.effect: LLM-simplified explanations rated easier, clearer, and more comprehensible in both experiments; all P<.05, r=0.11-0.24.
links.quote: Mann-Whitney U tests further showed that LLM-simplified explanations were rated as easier, clearer, and more comprehensible than the original versions in both experiments (all P<.05), with small to moderate effect sizes (r=0.11-0.24).

links.effect: 3 board-certified psychiatrists confirmed simplified content avoided factual errors or misinterpretations.
links.quote: This expert validation confirmed that the simplified content faithfully preserved the original medical meaning, avoided factual errors or misinterpretations, and presented information in a logically coherent manner.
